title: Polish 6/7: Send+Sync guarantee (assertion + concurrency test) and FFI design doc
description:
### Summary
Pin the crate's core FFI premise — `Ephemeris: Send + Sync` with no interior mutability — via a compile-time assertion and a real concurrency test, and write docs/ffi-design.md recording the C-ABI layer decision for the future Dart binding (successor to swisseph.dart). The FFI layer itself is NOT implemented here — this task makes the decision durable and the precondition enforced.

### Files
- `tests/send_sync.rs` (new) — or a module in an existing integration test target
- `docs/ffi-design.md` (new)

### Implementation steps
1. **Compile-time assertion**:
   ```rust
   fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
   #[test]
   fn ephemeris_is_send_sync() {
       assert_send_sync::<swisseph::Ephemeris>();
       assert_send_sync::<swisseph::EphemerisConfig>();
   }
   ```
   Verify it actually compiles today — Ephemeris fields are config + Vec<SwissEphFile> (memmap2::Mmap is Send+Sync) + Option<JplFile> + StarCatalog. If any field breaks the bound, STOP and report (that's an architecture violation, not something to patch around with unsafe impls).
2. **Concurrency determinism test** (same file): `std::thread::scope` with 8 threads sharing one `&Ephemeris` (Moshier config so it runs without data files), each computing calc_ut for all 10 planets at 100 epochs; join and assert every thread's results are bitwise-identical to a serially computed baseline (compare f64 bits, not epsilon). This is the "zero synchronization, identical answers" guarantee in executable form.
3. **docs/ffi-design.md** — record these decisions with rationale (they are MADE, the doc's job is to persist them and their reasoning):
   - **Approach: hand-rolled C ABI + cbindgen-generated header, in a separate `swisseph-ffi` crate (cdylib, workspace member added when the Dart work starts). NOT flutter_rust_bridge.** Rationale: the API is flat numeric data (f64 arrays, i32 codes, UTF-8 names) with no async/streams/callbacks — frb's codegen+runtime buys nothing here; the consumer (swisseph.dart successor) already speaks dart:ffi against the C Swiss Ephemeris ABI, so a hand-controlled ABI can mirror shapes that binding already handles; raw-pointer-as-int isolate sharing needs a stable, auditable ABI surface, not generated glue that owns the handle model. Rejected alternative recorded: flutter_rust_bridge — revisit only if the Dart side ever needs streams/async event search.
   - **Handle model**: `swisseph_new(config…) -> *mut Ephemeris` via Box::into_raw; Dart isolates pass the pointer as an int (Dart can't send objects across isolates but can send ints); every calc call takes the handle + params; `swisseph_free(*mut Ephemeris)` via Box::from_raw, registered with Dart NativeFinalizer. Config is immutable after construction — NO set_* mutators in the ABI; per-call variance (topo position, sidereal mode) rides as explicit call parameters mapping to the existing `*_with_config` pattern.
   - **Error convention**: i32 return codes (0 = OK, negative = error, mirroring C's retflag < 0 convention) + out-params for results; an error-code enum mapped 1:1 from `swisseph::Error` variants + a `swisseph_last_error_message(handle_or_threadlocal…)`-free design — prefer a `char* err_buf, usize err_cap` out-param per call (stateless, isolate-safe) over any thread-local last-error.
   - **Type flattening table**: CalcResult → `double xx[6]` + `int32 flags_used` out-params; enums → i32 with the existing C constant values (Body already mirrors ipl numbering via as_c_int-style mapping); &str star names → UTF-8 `const char*` in, caller-allocated buffer out.
   - **What the lib crate must uphold** (this is the contract the assertion test enforces): Send+Sync, no interior mutability ever added to Ephemeris (any future cache must be a separate opt-in wrapper type), `#[repr]`-stability not required on Rust types (FFI crate defines its own #[repr(C)] mirrors).
   - Cross-reference: the capstone N-isolates-vs-copy-per-isolate benchmark lives in the benchmarks task (Polish 7/7).

### C reference
None.

### Golden tests
None — the concurrency test asserts internal consistency (parallel == serial, bitwise), not C parity.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --test send_sync` (or the chosen target) passes, including the 8-thread bitwise-determinism test
- `cargo test` passes
- docs/ffi-design.md exists and contains the decision, rationale, rejected alternative, handle model, and error convention sections

### Escape hatch
If `Ephemeris` fails the Send+Sync bound, STOP immediately and report which field and why — do not add `unsafe impl Send/Sync` under any circumstances.
execution_record: Uneventful — Ephemeris/EphemerisConfig passed the Send+Sync bound on first compile (no interior mutability anywhere, escape hatch never triggered). tests/send_sync.rs: compile-time assertion + 8-thread scope test, 10 planets × 100 epochs (1900–2037, 500-day steps, MOSEPH|SPEED), results compared as raw f64 bits ([u64;6] + flags_used bits) against a serial baseline — all threads bitwise-identical. docs/ffi-design.md written with all required sections (decision + rationale + rejected frb alternative, handle model, error convention, flattening table, lib-crate contract, Polish 7/7 cross-ref). cargo test: all 5 targets pass.
